newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MTBE rises but bearish hues seen on horizon.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MTBE rises but bearish hues seen on horizon.

text.p: U.S. spot MTBE prices rose sharply this week amid refiner and trader buying but the start-up of the huge plant in Saudi Arabia put a bearish note to the market, players said Wednesday.

The new 16,000 barrel per day (bpd) plant in Saudi Arabia began producing on-spec barrels on Monday following several false starts and is at 60 percent capacity, said a source close to Saudi Petrochemical Co (Sadaf).
Sadaf is a joint venture between Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC) and Shell Oil Co, with each partner owning a 50 percent stake.

"When those barrels start coming in in early July we may see prices start to drop," said a U.S. MTBE broker. According to industry players, about 70 percent of Sadaf production is to be marketed in the U.S.
Prompt supplies in the U.S., however, remain tight due to plant problems earlier this year and current high production rates for gasoline that has pulled on the MTBE pool.
In Houston, prompt June sold for 85.00 cents a gallon Tuesday and Wednesday, a three cent increase from Monday. A 30,000-barrel parcel traded hands at 85.00 cents on Wednesday.
In New York, much of June was considered finished. Prompt July traded at 88.00 cents on Wednesday.
Meanwhile, traders said ARCO Chemical's Rotterdam facility has begun coming back up from turnaround this month. The plant is a significant importer of MTBE into the Harbor.
-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk 1212-859-1631 --
